issues.description: Method Developer.attend(course:) has inconsistent parameter types across artifacts. The problem statement (problem_statement.md) and the template implementation (Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift in the template) specify the parameter as an optional Course? and instruct students to use optional binding. The solution implementation (Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift in the solution) declares the method as attend(course: Course) with a non-optional parameter. This mismatch hides the nil-handling/optional-binding behavior the exercise asks students to implement and can confuse students when they compare their optional-binding-based solution and the provided reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution's attend method to accept an optional Course? and use optional binding to unwrap it, matching the problem statement and template. For example, in the solution change the signature to `func attend(course: Course?) { if let course = course { ... } }` and keep the existing logic inside the unwrapping block; also add behavior (or explicit no-op) for the nil case if desired.
